papers.title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
papers.reason: metric depth estimation；可将船舶单目相对深度先验通过分段仿射尺度恢复转换为度量深度，并利用稀疏船舶测距或雷达深度观测沿最小几何变化路径进行像素级传播；需要将16个通用数据集的训
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/MTD upon publication.
papers.abstract_zh: 最近的基础模型大大改进了对单体相对深度估计的概括性,但由于尺度模糊和地方尺度不一致,从其深度感知任务估计中恢复准确的度量深度仍然具有挑战性。 现有方法利用明显的全球近缘变换算法或暗含的数据驱动深度完成网络,从稀少的观测中恢复测量深度。 前者不能适应空间差异的相对对度量关系,而后者对稀有观测的分布很敏感,可能无法充分利用可概括的相对深度前传. 为了同时解决这些问题,本研究报告扩展了我们先前的工作。 MTD 和提议 MTDv2, 混合度量衡深度感知框架,将明确度量衡与数据驱动的度量深度完善相结合. 清晰的深度测量过程进行断面近缘变换,以恢复空间变化的计量尺度,同时保持相对深度的几何结构,然后对像素深度进行精细调整,沿最小的累积几何变化的路径传播计量观测结果。 数据驱动的深度改进过程随后将明确的单路径深度传播扩大到可学习的多路径配方,同时保持其可解释性。 在下列领域进行了广泛的实验: 16 公共数据集显示有强大和一般的深度尺度回收能力 MTDv2 不同的观测来源和不同的深度估计范式,及其广泛适用于下游 3D 认知任务。 代码将在 https://mias.group/MTD 发表时.

papers.title: SARFusion: Scene-Aware Routing Fusion for Robust Camera-LiDAR 3D Object Detection
papers.reason: robust camera-LiDAR 3D object detection via scene-aware branch routing fusion；可设想把场景可靠性先验与逐查询分支路由移植到
papers.abstract: Camera-LiDAR fusion has become a prevailing paradigm for 3D object detection in autonomous driving. However, existing fusion detectors often establish strong inter-modality dependencies by decoding object queries from tightly coupled multimodal representations. Under corrupted driving conditions, such dependencies make the detector vulnerable to unreliable modalities, where degraded observations may interfere with reliable modality-specific evidence and lead to suboptimal predictions. Moreover, modality reliability can vary across both global driving scenes and individual object queries, requiring adaptive fusion decisions at a finer granularity. To bridge this gap, we reformulate robust camera-LiDAR fusion as a scene-aware branch routing problem and propose SARFusion, a robust 3D object detector. Instead of producing detections from a single fused representation, SARFusion decouples object-query decoding into three parallel reasoning branches: a camera branch, a LiDAR branch, and a camera-LiDAR fusion branch. Guided by a Scene Reliability Prior estimated from the global driving context, SARFusion further incorporates object-level evidence to route each query to the most suitable branch. This query-wise routing strategy alleviates harmful cross-modal interference while preserving the benefits of multimodal fusion when complementary cues are trustworthy. On the nuScenes test set, SARFusion achieves strong performance with 72.5 mAP and 74.4 NDS. Extensive analyses demonstrate its robustness under challenging conditions, including sensor corruptions and environmental changes.

papers.title: When LiDAR Fades, Radar Takes Over: LiDAR Reliability-Aware Adaptive Localization Under Airborne Obscurants
papers.reason: LiDAR退化检测与雷达/LiDAR自适应定位；可将LiDAR可靠性估计门控从定位模态切换调整为多传感器检测中的视觉/雷达分支加权或切换：输入改为各传感器检测特征及质量线索，训练目标改为正常/退化状态
papers.abstract: LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO) is widely used for real-time localization and mapping, but its reliability can degrade substantially in subterranean environments affected by smoke, dust, and other airborne obscurants, whereas radar remains comparatively robust. This article presents a one-class temporal learning framework for LiDAR degradation detection and reliability-aware localization under such conditions. A broad set of degradation-sensitive cues, including spatial, cross-modal, geometric/motion, intensity, and measurement-recency features, is evaluated to characterize changes in LiDAR sensing quality. Their temporal evolution is modelled over sliding windows using an LSTM autoencoder trained exclusively on nominal operation, enabling deviations from healthy sensor behaviour to be detected without requiring labelled degradation data. The resulting LiDAR reliability estimate governs adaptive selection between LIO and radar inertial odometry (RIO), retaining LIO during reliable sensing and transferring localization authority to RIO when degradation is detected. The framework is evaluated using real-world ground robot data collected in GNSS-denied subterranean tunnels under nominal and dense-smoke conditions. Experimental results demonstrate degradation detection, adaptive modality switching, and continued localization output under severe LiDAR degradation. A feature family ablation study further shows that a reduced feature representation can improve degradation-aware localization performance in the evaluated dense-smoke scenarios, highlighting the importance of feature parsimony in one-class sensor degradation detection. The code will be released as open source to support reproducibility and further research.

papers.title: TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities
papers.reason: cross_modal_matching；将轻量模态适配模块用于视觉–AIS或Radar–AIS跨模态匹配：保留共享匹配主干，为AIS/雷达增加模态适配层；若无配对真值，可用仿真或按轨迹关联构造合成对
papers.abstract: Robotic platforms combine multi-modal sensors to operate across diverse conditions, but most dense correspondence methods are limited to RGB-RGB or a small set of modality pairs. Training a model for each modality pair scales poorly with the number of sensors and forgoes potential positive transfer across modality pairs. We introduce TartanMatch, a unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered pairs among RGB, event, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR. TartanMatch adapts an RGB-pretrained correspondence model to all modality pairs within one shared network using lightweight modality adaptation and a mixture of real and synthetic data. On zero-shot real-world benchmarks, TartanMatch reduces Endpoint Error (EPE) over the strongest baselines by 61.9% for cross-modal matching and 49.6% for same-modal matching. We further show that joint training across all modality pairs improves average matching accuracy over pair-specific training, especially on challenging cross-modal pairs. These results demonstrate that a single model achieves broad multi-modal coverage and state-of-the-art matching accuracy.

papers.title: ReDiffNet: Differential RGB-Infrared Learning for Low-Light UAV Oriented Vehicle Detection
papers.reason: RGB-infrared low-light vehicle detection；将RGB-红外两模态可靠性选择与差分恢复机制，调整到雷达/视觉或AIS/视觉多传感器船舶检测：输入改为雷达点云或AIS
papers.abstract: Low-light UAV-based RGB-infrared oriented small-vehicle detection is important for nighttime traffic monitoring, emergency response, and urban inspection. Illumination variations, headlight glare, local shadows, and thermal-response degradation cause spatially varying modality reliability, while the small visual extent of vehicles further weakens boundaries, orientation cues, and thermal responses. Accordingly, selecting trustworthy observations based on local modality reliability while further exploiting complementary discriminative information in regions with ambiguous modality preference is key to constructing effective multimodal representations. Based on this insight, we propose ReDiffNet, a reliability-conditioned differential representation network in which modality reliability guides both evidence selection and complementary recovery. Specifically, degradation-aware reliability learning estimates relative spatial reliability, uncertainty-guided differential recovery exploits cross-modal differences to recover complementary cues in ambiguous regions, and reliability-conditioned reconstruction integrates retained and recovered evidence into a unified representation. ReDiffNet achieves 85.3% and 73.9% mAP50 on DroneVehicle and VEDAI, respectively, supporting its effectiveness.

ReDiffNet 实现 85.3% 和 73.9% mAP50 在 DroneVehicle 和 VEDAI, 分别支持其有效性.
